bottleneck.evidence: The audited frozen result was correct and neutral at both M buckets with zero wins and zero regressions; production profiling separately identified a one-wave, shared-memory-limited TMA pipeline dominated by scoreboard and barrier waiting.

approaches.summary: Added an isolated SM100 DeepGEMM entry that consumes production int32 packed UE8M0 scales directly and stages scale words in the transposer warp.
approaches.why: Replacing stock scale TMAs with ordinary warp loads and shared stores increased device instructions and synchronization work.

approaches.summary: Specialized the fixed q_b N and K dimensions while preserving the production packed ABI.
approaches.why: Removing dynamic dimensions did not offset the extra scale-staging work.

approaches.summary: Prefetched packed words across the A/B barrier, vectorized shared stores, restored the stock SM count, and broadcast the uniform weight scale from lane zero.
approaches.why: The final kernel remained slower in graph replay at both production buckets even after reducing redundant loads.

lesson: For tiny-M SM100 DeepGEMM, a faster Python submission path can look like a large CUDA-event win while the underlying kernel is slower. Always validate with CUDA Graph replay and NCU; moving tiny scale transfers from TMA to a consumer warp can add more shared-store and scoreboard cost than it removes.
transfers_to: SM100 tiny-M FP8 linear kernels using TMA-aligned UE8M0 scales

caveats: The frozen result is PROVISIONAL because the evidence tree was uncommitted during evaluation; candidate and frozen harness files were clean.
The frozen task uses f32 block scales and is not the production packed-int32 ABI.
